note: Intro captions, in display order. Source of truth for the caption list in index.html: run `npm run build-copy` after editing, `npm run check-copy` to validate. Rules (plan section 6): every fact carries source_url, retrieved and verify_before_ship; dated facts carry as_of; computed values are filled from data/map.json, never typed. `npm run check-copy -- --ship` additionally fails on any verify_before_ship: true or an unapproved CTA.

captions.text: The Arkansas, Colorado, Platte, and Rio Grande all begin in Colorado.
captions.source_label: Water Education Colorado, Major River Basins
captions.notes: Plan: verified, quote "the Arkansas, Colorado, Platte, and the Rio Grande".

captions.text: Most of Colorado's rivers begin in the Rocky Mountains and flow across state lines.
captions.source_label: Water Education Colorado, Major River Basins

captions.text: The Colorado River supplies more than 40 million people in seven states and Mexico.
captions.source_label: Water Education Colorado, Colorado River Basin
captions.notes: Plan: verified. Optional 75% add not used: per a 2026-10-16 search summary the full sentence is 'less than 20 percent of the entire Colorado River Basin lies inside Colorado, but about 75 percent of the water that feeds the river originates here', attributed to the 2015 Colorado Water Plan. Read the page itself before adding it.

captions.text: Water from these four systems crosses {statesCrossed} states.
captions.derived_from: data/map.json: states with at least 3 river vertices inside the state polygon (scripts/check-copy.mjs, statesCrossed)
captions.notes: Definition needs sign-off. Counts states a drawn river passes through, Colorado included. Not counted: states the water only borders (the Colorado River along California and Nevada, the Platte terminus on the Iowa/Missouri side), and Mississippi, which the Arkansas line touches with 2 vertices at its confluence (a state-boundary artifact; the map still fades Mississippi in at that moment).

captions.text: Denver Water reports natural streamflow ran at 22% of normal from April through July, the lowest in 110 years.
captions.notes: Open: confirm geographic scope (Denver Water supply basins vs statewide) and word the caption to match. The 22% figure did not appear in 2026-10-16 search summaries; Denver Water's Oct. 12 update cites runoff forecasts of 10-40% of normal. source_url is Denver Water's article on the Aug. 26 action; confirm it carries the figure or replace it with the resolution document.

captions.text: Lake Powell and Lake Mead have reached record-low combined storage.
captions.notes: Single secondary source. Verify against Reclamation (24-Month Study or operations data) before ship.

captions.text: On August 21, Reclamation set a two-year operating plan for 2027–2028 inside a ten-year framework. Lower Basin cuts are mandatory: 1.25 million acre-feet per year. Upper Basin participation is voluntary.
captions.source_label: Bureau of Reclamation, Record of Decision; Western Water, Aug. 21, 2026
captions.notes: Confirm figures in the ROD PDF. The ten-year framework does not lock in amounts for the decade.

captions.text: On August 26, Denver Water ordered lawn watering to end October 1, through at least spring 2027. Hand-watering of trees and gardens is still allowed.
captions.notes: Plan: verified 2026-09-20. Dated; re-check before each deploy (the ban runs until the board decides how and when watering resumes).

captions.text: On September 4, the Colorado PUC cut Xcel's requested gas rate increase from $190 million to $122.7 million a year. New rates take effect October 6.
captions.source_label: Colorado PUC press release, Sept. 4, 2026, Proceeding 25AL-0538G
captions.notes: Plan: verified 2026-09-20. Re-check before ship: 'take effect October 6' is future tense and that date has passed; the final written decision (about Oct. 1) opened a 20-day reconsideration window.

captions.text: Three exposures: the interstate compact, the utility, the local supply. A ratepayer carries the second whatever happens to the first.
captions.notes: Project analytical frame (three axes). Framing, not a factual claim; closing statement before the CTA.

cta.text: Everyone downstream of these decisions is affected: people who drink this water, farm with it, heat homes with the gas, and pay the bills. This is the record.
cta.notes: Editorial. Jamison to approve wording. Rendered in M5.
